```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(AKCatchments)
options(AKCatchments.cache = file.path(tempdir(), "ak_vignette_cache"))
```

Catchment summaries of the 30 m probability of permafrost within 1 m of the
surface (Pastick et al. 2015; USGS data release doi:10.5066/F7C53HX6;
about 2001-2010), an alternate to the Jorgenson extent classes
(`vignette("permafrost-jorgenson")`). Values 0-100 are probabilities;
101-105 are masked NLCD 2001 classes (water, ice and snow, developed,
barren, cultivated).

Input, as for every layer: catchments (sf polygons with `site_code`, one
row per catchment, any CRS; a single `ak_delineate()` result, a list of
them, `ak_catchments()` output or your own polygons). Chunks that download
data are not run when this vignette is built; chunks that only compute
are. The other layers are listed in `vignette("delineation")`, section 7.

## 1. Getting the data

Automatic, once: a 7-Zip archive (777 MB, holding a `.tar`) from
ScienceBase into the cache's `pastick_2015/` folder. Unpacking needs the
`archive` R package or a 7z program; archives found inside are unpacked in
place and deleted, so a cache left with only the `.tar` recovers without
downloading again.

```{r prefetch, eval = FALSE}
ak_prefetch(x, layers = "permafrost/pastick2015")
```

## 2. Using it

```{r use, eval = FALSE}
d <- ak_delineate(lat = 63.7255, lon = -148.9670, site_code = "SITE-001")   # one catchment
ak_permafrost(d, source = "pastick2015")                  # one catchment

x <- ak_catchments(pts)                                  # many: data frame of site_code, lat, lon
x <- ak_permafrost(x, source = "pastick2015")              # columns appended to x, provenance recorded
ak_provenance(x)

ak_permafrost(sf::read_sf("hand_catchments.gpkg"), source = "pastick2015")   # your own polygons
```

## 3. What you get

`pf_prob_mean` (mean probability over the vegetated part), `pf_extent_pct`
(share above 50%), `pf_land_lo` / `pf_land_hi` (permafrost over all
non-glacier, non-water land with masked land counted as none / all
permafrost), `pf_masked_pct`, `pf_icesnow_pct`, `pf_barren_pct`,
`pf_coverage_pct`, `pf_flag` (`partial_coverage` under 90% mapped,
`mostly_masked` over 25% masked).

## 4. Uncertainty: how it is computed

**Product error.** About 85% accuracy at the 50% threshold, likely lower
for small areas; no per-pixel error layer. Errors are correlated within a
catchment, so no SE is given.

**What is reported.** `pf_prob_mean` (mean probability over the vegetated
part: the expected permafrost fraction if the probabilities are
calibrated), `pf_extent_pct` (share above 50%: more sensitive to
misclassification near the threshold), and bounds `pf_land_lo` /
`pf_land_hi` treating masked land (barren, developed) as none or all
permafrost. `pf_flag` marks partial coverage and mostly masked catchments.

## 5. Checking and validating it

Compare with Jorgenson (see `vignette("permafrost-jorgenson")`, section
5), and check `pf_masked_pct`: in glaciated and rocky WRST catchments much
of the area is masked, and `pf_prob_mean` then describes a small vegetated
part. The bounds `pf_land_lo`-`pf_land_hi` say how much that matters.

## 6. Pitfalls

- It is a model output whose predictors include climate, terrain and
  vegetation: in a causal analysis it sits downstream of them.
- Static (~2001-2010): no thaw since.
- Within 1 m only: the layer for shallow flow paths, not deep permafrost.

## References

- Pastick, N. J. et al. (2015). Distribution of near-surface permafrost in Alaska: estimates of present and future conditions. Remote Sensing of Environment 168, 301-315. Data: doi:10.5066/F7C53HX6.
